A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOTIF research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConnectHub experiments, knowledge-graph link-prediction results, motif ablations, and scalability measurements in Tables 1-4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including synthetic accuracy, zero-shot and fine-tuned link prediction, end-to-end training, and scalability measurements.

M1.justification: The MOTIF pipeline, encoder update rules, experimental architecture, and training loss are retained. Section 5 newly states the invariant-initialization requirement for representing the INGRAM variant, clarifying its inclusion without establishing a changed MOTIF procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ConnectHub tasks, three pretraining graphs, 51 transfer-evaluation graphs, and 54-graph end-to-end evaluation. The newly discussed Metafam and WIKITOPICS-MT results already appear in v1's appendix tables.

E2.justification: ULTRA and the evaluated MOTIF variants remain the same within corresponding comparisons. The expanded TRIX discussion is theoretical; v2 adds no experimental TRIX comparator.

E3.justification: The splits, inverse-edge augmentation, filtered-ranking metrics, prediction directions, training budgets, and model configurations are unchanged. Tables 6 and 13-17 retain the dataset and training settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same motif ablations, ConnectHub tests, WN-v2 embedding-degradation case study, and scalability analysis. The added domain-specific paragraph summarizes existing benchmark results rather than introducing a distinct diagnostic or robustness evaluation.

E5.justification: Both report three-run averages for fine-tuning and end-to-end experiments, with unchanged uncertainty entries in Tables 9-12. No new seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Tabulated measurements are unchanged, but Section 7.2 newly reports WIKITOPICS-MT subgroup averages: ULTRA/MOTIF MRR 0.331/0.358 and Hits@10 0.442/0.481, derived from existing Table 7 rows. Its new claim of 58% improvement on MT1-tax conflicts with that table's MRR values, 0.224 and 0.325, which imply about 45%.

T1.justification: New Appendix B adds two explicit graph constructions and reasoning for TRIX/MOTIF expressivity incomparability. Section 5 also makes the INGRAM invariance qualification explicit. The existing WL characterization, principal theorems, and their proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general motif framework, an expressivity analysis, conditions for richer motifs to increase separation power, and empirical validation across diverse knowledge graphs.

C2.justification: v2 explains MOTIF's motif-existence mechanism against TRIX's occurrence-counting mechanism and presents their capabilities as complementary. Section 7.2 newly connects existing Metafam and WIKITOPICS-MT results to complex relational patterns. The previous scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 7.2 replaces the anonymous code-hosting link with an author-associated GitHub MOTIF link. The documented architectures, sparse-matrix and Triton implementations, hardware, and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 2 newly credits TRIX as the first work comparing KGFM expressivity. Appendix B substantially clarifies this particular relationship by arguing incomparability and complementary strengths, without broadly restructuring the related-work coverage.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory examples for invariants, expands the LIFT description into bullets, formats the research questions as a list, and inserts a dedicated TRIX appendix. Copyediting and acknowledgment placement also change, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: New main-text Figure 6 repeats the three-path motifs already shown in v1's appendix Figure 9, retained as v2 Figure 10. Other figures and tables are relocated or reflowed; their substantive displays, including the relation-similarity heatmap, are unchanged.

improvement.justification: More explicit theoretical scope, clearer LIFT explanations, and updated code-access information provide a limited net improvement while preserving the original evidence. These gains are qualified by new errors: Section 7.2 overstates the MT1-tax gain as 58% rather than about 45%, and Section 4.1 introduces a repeated r_n index in its hyperedge tuple.
